source.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל־הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Moses was shepherding [the] flock of Jethro his father-in-law, [the] priest of Midian, and he drove the flock behind the wilderness and came to [the] mountain of God, to Horeb.

en.L: And Moses was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he drove the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
en.B: Moses was looking after the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock deep into the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
en.R: Moses took care of the sheep and goats that belonged to his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. One day Moses led the animals far into the desert. He came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

es.L: Y Moisés estaba pastoreando el rebaño de Jetro, su suegro, el sacerdote de Madián; y llevó el rebaño al otro lado del desierto y llegó al monte de Dios, a Horeb.
es.B: Moisés cuidaba el rebaño de su suegro Jetro, el sacerdote de Madián. Llevó el rebaño hasta lo más lejano del desierto y llegó a Horeb, el monte de Dios.
es.R: Moisés cuidaba las ovejas y las cabras de su suegro Jetro, el sacerdote de Madián. Un día llevó los animales muy lejos, al desierto. Así llegó a Horeb, el monte de Dios.

fr.L: Et Moïse faisait paître le troupeau de Jéthro, son beau-père, le prêtre de Madian ; et il mena le troupeau à l’autre bout du désert et vint à la montagne de Dieu, à l’Horeb.
fr.B: Moïse gardait le troupeau de son beau-père Jéthro, le prêtre de Madian. Il conduisit le troupeau loin dans le désert et arriva à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.
fr.R: Moïse s’occupait des moutons et des chèvres de son beau-père Jéthro, le prêtre de Madian. Un jour, il a emmené les bêtes loin dans le désert. Il est arrivé à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.

sw.L: Naye Musa alikuwa akichunga kundi la Yethro baba mkwe wake, kuhani wa Midiani; akaliongoza kundi hadi upande wa mbali wa nyika, akafika kwenye mlima wa Mungu, Horebu.
sw.B: Musa alikuwa akichunga kundi la baba mkwe wake Yethro, kuhani wa Midiani. Akaliongoza kundi mbali ndani ya nyika, akafika Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa akiwatunza kondoo na mbuzi wa baba mkwe wake Yethro, kuhani wa Midiani. Siku moja Musa aliwapeleka wanyama hao mbali jangwani. Akafika Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: Jethro: the priest of Midian, called Reuel in 2:18
decisions.reason: The same man has two names in Exodus (2:18; 3:1). He may have had a personal name and a title, or Reuel may be the name of his clan.

decisions.choice: behind the wilderness: to the far side of the wilderness, or westward into it
alternatives: to the west side of the wilderness
decisions.reason: "Behind" can mean "beyond", or "west", since a Hebrew speaker faced east to give directions. Either way, Moses went far from the usual pastures.

decisions.choice: the mountain of God, Horeb: the mountain called Sinai elsewhere
decisions.reason: Horeb and Sinai are names for the same mountain (compare 19:11 with Deuteronomy 5:2). The narrator calls it "the mountain of God" because of what happens there; its location is not certain.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: The "wilderness" is dry, empty land used for grazing. Readable uses the common word.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("il mena", "arriva"); passé composé at Readable ("il a emmené", "il est arrivé")
decisions.reason: The passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. The ongoing shepherding at the start is in the imperfect ("faisait paître", "gardait") at every level.

source.text: וַ֠יֵּרָא מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו בְּלַבַּת־אֵ֖שׁ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַסְּנֶה֙ בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְהַסְּנֶ֖ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֻכָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared [the] angel of Yahweh to him in [a] flame of fire from [the] midst of the bush, and he looked, and look, the bush [was] burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. And he looked, and look, the bush was burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
en.B: There the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him in a flame of fire coming out of a bush. Moses looked, and although the bush was ablaze, it was not burning away.
en.R: There the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him in a fire that was burning inside a bush. Moses looked closely. The bush was on fire, but the fire did not destroy it.

es.L: Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció en una llama de fuego desde el medio de la zarza. Y miró, y he aquí que la zarza estaba ardiendo con fuego, y la zarza no quedaba consumida.
es.B: Allí el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció en una llama de fuego que salía de una zarza. Moisés miró, y aunque la zarza estaba en llamas, el fuego no la consumía.
es.R: Allí el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a él en un fuego que ardía dentro de una zarza. Moisés miró con atención. La zarza estaba en llamas, pero el fuego no la destruía.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut dans une flamme de feu, du milieu du buisson. Et il regarda, et voici, le buisson était en feu, et le buisson n’était pas dévoré.
fr.B: Là, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut dans une flamme de feu qui sortait d’un buisson. Moïse regarda : le buisson flambait, et pourtant il ne se consumait pas.
fr.R: Là, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est venu vers lui dans un feu qui brûlait au milieu d’un buisson. Moïse a regardé attentivement. Le buisson était en feu, mais le feu ne le détruisait pas.

sw.L: Na malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea katika mwali wa moto kutoka katikati ya kichaka. Akatazama, na tazama, kichaka kilikuwa kikiwaka moto, na kichaka hakikuungua.
sw.B: Huko malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea katika mwali wa moto uliokuwa ukitoka kichakani. Musa akatazama, akaona kwamba ingawa kichaka kilikuwa kikiwaka, hakikuteketea.
sw.R: Huko malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjia katika moto uliokuwa ukiwaka ndani ya kichaka. Musa akatazama kwa makini. Kichaka kilikuwa kinawaka moto, lakini moto haukukiharibu.

decisions.choice: the angel of Yahweh: God's messenger, in whom God himself is present
decisions.reason: The word means "messenger". In the next verses it is God himself who speaks from the bush (verses 4-6), as with the angel in Genesis 16:7-13 and 22:11-16. The text does not explain how the messenger and God are related.

decisions.choice: the bush: a thorny desert shrub
decisions.reason: The word is used only here and in Deuteronomy 33:16. It sounds like "Sinai", the name of the mountain, a link that may be intended.

decisions.choice: flame of fire: fire marks God's presence
decisions.reason: Fire goes with God's appearances: the smoking firepot (Genesis 15:17), the pillar of fire (13:21), and the fire on Sinai (19:18).

decisions.choice: angel
decisions.reason: "Angel" is the familiar word for God's heavenly messenger. "Messenger" is given in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "n'était pas dévoré"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "to eat": fire "eats" what it burns. Literal keeps the picture with "dévoré"; Balanced uses the usual "se consumer".

decisions.choice: "kichaka" (bush, shrub)
decisions.reason: The word is a thorny desert shrub (m2). "Kichaka" is the everyday word for a bush; "kijiti" suggests a small stick or sapling.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה־נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא־יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses, let me turn aside and see this great sight, why does not burn the bush?

en.L: And Moses said, "Let me turn aside, please, and see this great sight, why the bush does not burn up."
en.B: Moses said, "I must turn aside and look at this remarkable sight. Why is the bush not burning away?"
en.R: Moses said to himself, "This is amazing! I will go over and look at it. Why does the bush not burn up?"

es.L: Y dijo Moisés: «Voy a apartarme, pues, y ver este gran espectáculo: por qué no se consume la zarza».
es.B: Moisés dijo: «Tengo que acercarme a mirar esto tan extraordinario. ¿Por qué la zarza no se quema del todo?».
es.R: Moisés se dijo: «¡Qué asombroso! Voy a ir a verlo de cerca. ¿Por qué no se quema la zarza?».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit : « Je vais donc faire un détour et voir ce grand spectacle : pourquoi le buisson ne brûle pas. »
fr.B: Moïse dit : « Il faut que je fasse un détour pour regarder ce spectacle extraordinaire. Pourquoi le buisson ne se consume-t-il pas ? »
fr.R: Moïse s’est dit : « C’est étonnant ! Je vais m’approcher pour regarder. Pourquoi le buisson ne brûle-t-il pas jusqu’au bout ? »

sw.L: Musa akasema, "Na nigeuke kando sasa, nikaone jambo hili kubwa, kwa nini kichaka hakiungui."
sw.B: Musa akasema, "Lazima niende kando nikaangalie jambo hili la ajabu. Kwa nini kichaka hiki hakiteketei?"
sw.R: Musa akajiambia, "Hili ni la kushangaza! Nitakwenda kuliangalia. Kwa nini kichaka hakiungui?"

decisions.choice: turn aside: leave his path to go and look
decisions.reason: Verse 4 uses the same verb: God speaks when he sees that Moses has turned aside. The meeting begins with Moses' curiosity.

decisions.choice: said to himself
decisions.reason: No one else is present, so Moses is speaking to himself.

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י סָ֣ר לִרְא֑וֹת וַיִּקְרָא֩ אֵלָ֨יו אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֗ה וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Yahweh that he turned aside to see, and called to him God from [the] midst of the bush and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, here I [am].

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that he turned aside to see, and God called to him from the midst of the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he said, "Here I [am]."
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that he had come over to look, God called out to him from the bush: "Moses! Moses!" "Yes, I am here," he answered.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Moses had come to look. So God called to him from inside the bush, "Moses! Moses!" Moses answered, "Yes, I am here."

es.L: Y vio {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que se apartaba para mirar, y Dios lo llamó de en medio de la zarza y dijo: «¡Moisés, Moisés!». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy».
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que Moisés se había acercado a mirar, Dios lo llamó desde la zarza: «¡Moisés! ¡Moisés!». «Sí, aquí estoy», respondió él.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio que Moisés se acercaba a mirar. Entonces Dios lo llamó desde dentro de la zarza: «¡Moisés! ¡Moisés!». Moisés respondió: «Sí, aquí estoy».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’il faisait un détour pour voir, et Dieu l’appela du milieu du buisson et dit : « Moïse, Moïse ! » Et il dit : « Me voici. »
fr.B: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vit qu’il s’était approché pour regarder, Dieu l’appela du buisson : « Moïse ! Moïse ! » « Oui, me voici », répondit-il.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a vu que Moïse venait regarder. Alors Dieu l’a appelé du milieu du buisson : « Moïse ! Moïse ! » Moïse a répondu : « Oui, je suis là. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba amegeuka kando ili kutazama, Mungu akamwita kutoka katikati ya kichaka, akasema, "Musa, Musa!" Naye akasema, "Mimi hapa."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoona kwamba amekuja kutazama, Mungu akamwita kutoka kichakani, "Musa! Musa!" Akajibu, "Naam, mimi hapa."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliona kwamba Musa amekuja kutazama. Basi Mungu akamwita kutoka ndani ya kichaka, "Musa! Musa!" Musa akajibu, "Naam, niko hapa."

decisions.choice: Yahweh ... God: the same one, called by both names
decisions.reason: The verse moves between the divine name and "God" without a change of subject. The name will be explained in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: here I am: an answer of readiness
decisions.reason: This is the answer of Abraham when God called him (Genesis 22:1, 11) and of Jacob (Genesis 46:2). It means "I am listening, ready."

decisions.choice: Moses, Moses: the name is said twice
decisions.reason: God calls Abraham, Jacob and Samuel the same way (Genesis 22:11; 46:2; 1 Samuel 3:10), at a moment that changes their lives.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תִּקְרַ֣ב הֲלֹ֑ם שַׁל־נְעָלֶ֨יךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עוֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו אַדְמַת־קֹ֖דֶשׁ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, do not come near here; take off your sandals from on your feet, for the place which you [are] standing on it is ground of holiness.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do not come near here. Take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is ground of holiness."
en.B: "Come no nearer," God said. "Remove your sandals from your feet, because the place where you stand is holy ground."
en.R: God said, "Do not come any closer. Take off your sandals. You are standing on holy ground, because I am here."

es.L: Y dijo: «No te acerques aquí. Quítate las sandalias de los pies, porque el lugar en el que tú estás de pie es tierra de santidad».
es.B: «No te acerques más», dijo Dios. «Quítate las sandalias de los pies, porque el lugar donde te encuentras es tierra santa».
es.R: Dios le dijo: «No te acerques más. Quítate las sandalias. Estás pisando tierra santa, porque yo estoy aquí».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Ne t’approche pas d’ici. Enlève tes sandales de tes pieds, car l’endroit où tu te tiens, c’est une terre de sainteté. »
fr.B: « Ne viens pas plus près, dit Dieu. Retire les sandales de tes pieds, car l’endroit où tu es debout est une terre sainte. »
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Ne t’approche pas plus. Enlève tes sandales. Tu es sur une terre sainte, parce que je suis ici. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Usisogee hapa. Vua makubazi yako kutoka miguuni mwako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama juu yake ni ardhi ya utakatifu."
sw.B: Mungu akasema, "Usikaribie zaidi. Vua makubazi yako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama ni ardhi takatifu."
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Usije karibu zaidi. Vua makubazi yako. Umesimama juu ya ardhi takatifu, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko hapa."

decisions.choice: holy ground: set apart because God is present
decisions.reason: The ground is not holy in itself; it is holy because God is there. This is the first time Exodus uses the word "holy". Joshua is given the same command in Joshua 5:15.

decisions.choice: take off your sandals: a sign of respect
decisions.reason: Removing sandals shows reverence. Israel's priests seem to have served barefoot in the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: God said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he said". Balanced and Readable name the speaker, avoiding a pronoun at the start of the sentence.

decisions.choice: because I am here
decisions.reason: Readable says why the ground is holy, which the context makes clear.

decisions.choice: "makubazi" (sandals)
decisions.reason: The word is sandals, the footwear of a shepherd. "Viatu" is shoes in general.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיַּסְתֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנָ֔יו כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א מֵהַבִּ֖יט אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, I [am the] God of your father, [the] God of Abraham, [the] God of Isaac and [the] God of Jacob. And hid Moses his face, for he was afraid of looking at God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I [am] the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
en.B: Then God said, "I am the God your father worshiped, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob." Moses covered his face, for he was afraid to look upon God.
en.R: God said, "I am the God your father worshiped. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." When Moses heard this, he hid his face. He was afraid to look at God.

es.L: Y dijo: «Yo [soy] el Dios de tu padre, el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob». Y Moisés se cubrió el rostro, porque tuvo miedo de mirar a Dios.
es.B: Luego Dios dijo: «Yo soy el Dios a quien adoraba tu padre, el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob». Moisés se tapó la cara, porque temía mirar a Dios.
es.R: Dios dijo: «Yo soy el Dios a quien adoraba tu padre. Soy el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob». Al oír esto, Moisés escondió la cara. Tenía miedo de mirar a Dios.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je [suis] le Dieu de ton père, le Dieu d’Abraham, le Dieu d’Isaac et le Dieu de Jacob. » Et Moïse se cacha le visage, car il avait peur de regarder Dieu.
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Je suis le Dieu que ton père adorait, le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob. » Moïse se couvrit le visage, car il craignait de regarder Dieu.
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Je suis le Dieu que ton père adorait. Je suis le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob. » Quand Moïse a entendu cela, il s’est caché le visage. Il avait peur de regarder Dieu.

sw.L: Akasema, "Mimi [ni] Mungu wa baba yako, Mungu wa Abrahamu, Mungu wa Isaka, na Mungu wa Yakobo." Naye Musa akajifunika uso, kwa sababu aliogopa kumtazama Mungu.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Mimi ni Mungu ambaye baba yako alimwabudu, Mungu wa Abrahamu, wa Isaka na wa Yakobo." Musa akajifunika uso wake, kwa kuwa aliogopa kumwangalia Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Mimi ni Mungu ambaye baba yako alimwabudu. Mimi ni Mungu wa Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo." Musa aliposikia hivyo, akaficha uso wake. Aliogopa kumtazama Mungu.

decisions.choice: your father: singular, Moses' own father, or the forefathers as one
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read the plural "your fathers", as in verses 13 and 15. The Hebrew singular may mean Moses' father Amram, or the line of fathers taken together.

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the God who made promises to them
decisions.reason: God names himself by the people he made his covenant with (2:24). Jesus quotes these words in Mark 12:26 to show that God is the God of the living.

decisions.choice: afraid to look at God: no one can see God and live
decisions.reason: Compare Genesis 32:30, Exodus 33:20 and Judges 13:22.

decisions.choice: the God your father worshiped
decisions.reason: "The God of your father" means the God whom your father served. Balanced and Readable say so, to avoid suggesting a family god owned by one man.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה רָאֹ֥ה רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־עֳנִ֥י עַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־צַעֲקָתָ֤ם שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י נֹֽגְשָׂ֔יו כִּ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־מַכְאֹבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, seeing I have seen [the] affliction of my people who [are] in Egypt, and their cry I have heard because of their taskmasters, for I know their pains.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have surely seen the affliction of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who [are] in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters, for I know their pains.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have taken full note of the misery of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt. I have heard them cry out under their taskmasters. I know how they are suffering.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I have seen how badly {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt are being treated. I have heard them crying out because of the cruel men who make them work. I know how much they are hurting.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «He visto, sí, he visto la aflicción de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo que [está] en Egipto, y he oído su clamor a causa de sus capataces, porque conozco sus dolores.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «He observado bien la miseria de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo en Egipto. He oído cómo gritan bajo sus capataces. Sé lo que están sufriendo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «He visto lo mal que tratan a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo en Egipto. Los he oído gritar por culpa de los hombres crueles que los obligan a trabajar. Sé cuánto están sufriendo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « J’ai bien vu l’affliction de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple qui [est] en Égypte, et j’ai entendu leur cri à cause de leurs chefs de corvée, car je connais leurs souffrances.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « J’ai pris pleinement connaissance de la misère de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je les ai entendus crier sous la contrainte de leurs chefs de corvée. Je sais combien ils souffrent.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : « J’ai vu comme on maltraite {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je les ai entendus crier à cause des hommes cruels qui les forcent à travailler. Je sais combien ils ont mal.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Kuona nimeona taabu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} walioko Misri, na kilio chao nimekisikia kwa sababu ya wanaowasukuma kazini, kwa kuwa ninajua uchungu wao.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Nimeiona kikamilifu dhiki ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} huko Misri. Nimewasikia wakilia chini ya wasimamizi wanaowalazimisha kazi. Ninajua jinsi wanavyoteseka.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Nimeona jinsi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wanavyoteswa huko Misri. Nimewasikia wakilia kwa sababu ya watu wakatili wanaowalazimisha kufanya kazi. Ninajua jinsi wanavyoumia.

decisions.choice: seeing I have seen: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Hebrew strengthens a verb by repeating it: "I have truly seen", "I have seen it all".

decisions.choice: seen ... heard ... know: God's answer to 2:24-25
decisions.reason: The verbs of 2:24-25 (heard, saw, knew) return, now spoken by God himself.

decisions.choice: my people: Israel belongs to God
decisions.reason: This is the first time God calls Israel "my people". It is the claim behind the demand to Pharaoh: "Let my people go" (5:1).

decisions.choice: taskmasters: drivers who forced the work
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who press or drive others to work; it is a different word from the officers of 1:11.

decisions.choice: "He visto, sí, he visto"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the doubled verb of the Hebrew (m1) by repeating it.

decisions.choice: "Kuona nimeona"
decisions.reason: Swahili can strengthen a verb by putting its infinitive before it, as Hebrew does (m1). Literal keeps the doubled verb.

source.text: וָאֵרֵ֞ד לְהַצִּיל֣וֹ׀מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֗יִם וּֽלְהַעֲלֹתוֹ֮ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִוא֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ טוֹבָה֙ וּרְחָבָ֔ה אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ אֶל־מְק֤וֹם הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have come down to deliver it from [the] hand of Egypt and to bring it up from that land to [a] land good and broad, to [a] land flowing [with] milk and honey, to [the] place of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.

en.L: And I have come down to deliver them from the hand of Egypt and to bring them up from that land to a good and broad land, to a land flowing [with] milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites.
en.B: I have come down to rescue them from the power of Egypt and to lead them up out of that country into a fine, wide land, a land flowing with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
en.R: So I have come down to save them from the Egyptians. I will lead them out of Egypt and bring them to a good land with plenty of room. It is a rich and fertile land, full of milk and honey. The Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live there now.

es.L: Y he descendido para librarlo de la mano de Egipto y para hacerlo subir de esa tierra a una tierra buena y amplia, a una tierra que fluye leche y miel, al lugar de los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.
es.B: He descendido para rescatarlos del poder de Egipto y sacarlos de ese país hacia una tierra buena y espaciosa, una tierra que fluye leche y miel, donde ahora viven los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.
es.R: Por eso he bajado para salvarlos de los egipcios. Los voy a sacar de Egipto y los llevaré a una tierra buena, con mucho espacio. Es una tierra rica y fértil, llena de leche y miel. Allí viven ahora los cananeos, los hititas, los amorreos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.

fr.L: Et je suis descendu pour le délivrer de la main de l’Égypte et pour le faire monter de ce pays-là vers un pays bon et vaste, vers un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, vers le lieu des Cananéens, des Hittites, des Amoréens, des Phéréziens, des Héviens et des Jébusiens.
fr.B: Je suis descendu pour le délivrer du pouvoir de l’Égypte et le faire monter de ce pays vers un pays bon et vaste, un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, là où vivent maintenant les Cananéens, les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens.
fr.R: Alors je suis descendu pour les sauver des Égyptiens. Je vais les faire sortir d’Égypte et les conduire dans un bon pays, où il y a beaucoup de place. C’est un pays riche et fertile, où coulent le lait et le miel. Les Cananéens, les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens y habitent maintenant.

sw.L: Nami nimeshuka ili kuwaokoa kutoka mkononi mwa Misri, na kuwapandisha kutoka nchi ile hadi nchi nzuri na pana, hadi nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, hadi mahali pa Wakanaani, na Wahiti, na Waamori, na Waperizi, na Wahivi, na Wayebusi.
sw.B: Nimeshuka ili kuwaokoa kutoka katika nguvu za Misri na kuwapandisha kutoka nchi ile kwenda nchi nzuri na yenye nafasi kubwa, nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, mahali wanapoishi sasa Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waamori, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nimeshuka ili niwaokoe kutoka kwa Wamisri. Nitawatoa Misri na kuwaleta katika nchi nzuri yenye nafasi tele. Ni nchi tajiri yenye rutuba, iliyojaa maziwa na asali. Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waamori, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi wanaishi huko sasa.

decisions.choice: I have come down: God acts in the world
decisions.reason: God "comes down" to see and to act (Genesis 11:5; 18:21). It does not mean God was absent before.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich land
decisions.reason: Milk from flocks and herds, and honey (wild bees' honey or syrup from dates or figs), stand for a land of plenty. This is the first of many times the phrase is used of Canaan.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites ... Jebusites: the peoples living in Canaan
decisions.reason: Lists like this one name the peoples of the land promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18-21). The names are singular in Hebrew, standing for each people as a whole.

decisions.choice: the hand of Egypt: Egypt's power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for control or power.

decisions.choice: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture before giving it.

decisions.choice: "le délivrer", "le faire monter" (singular, the people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular, referring to "my people" in verse 7. French keeps the singular with "peuple"; Readable says "les", the Israelites themselves.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הַלַּ֔חַץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹחֲצִ֥ים אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now look, [the] cry of [the] sons of Israel has come to me, and also I have seen the oppression which Egypt [is] oppressing them.

en.L: And now look, the cry of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel has come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
en.B: The outcry of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} has now reached {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have seen how harshly the Egyptians are crushing them.
en.R: Now I have heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And I have seen how cruelly the Egyptians are treating them.

decisions.choice: cry: an outcry for help against injustice
decisions.reason: The word is the cry of those wronged, as the outcry against Sodom (Genesis 18:20-21). Here it comes from the oppressed.

decisions.choice: the oppression ... oppressing: pressing, squeezing
decisions.reason: The verb means to press hard against (Numbers 22:25). The Egyptians are crushing Israel; the law forbids Israel to treat foreigners this way (22:21; 23:9).

decisions.choice: heard
decisions.reason: "The cry has come to me" means God has heard it. Readable says so.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְאֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֖ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְהוֹצֵ֛א אֶת־עַמִּ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now go, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring out my people, [the] sons of Israel, from Egypt.

en.L: And now, go, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, out of Egypt."
en.B: Go, then. I will send you to Pharaoh, and you are to bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of Egypt."
en.R: So now go. I am sending you to Pharaoh, the king. You will lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: I will send you ... bring out: God acts through Moses
decisions.reason: God says that he has come down to deliver Israel (verse 8), and that Moses will bring them out. Both are true: God works through the one he sends.

decisions.choice: bring out: the verb that gives the event its name
decisions.reason: "Bring out" of Egypt becomes the way the Old Testament speaks of the exodus (20:2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים מִ֣י אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אֵלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְכִ֥י אוֹצִ֛יא אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to God, who [am] I that I should go to Pharaoh and that I should bring out [the] sons of Israel from Egypt?

en.L: And Moses said to God, "Who [am] I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out of Egypt?"
en.B: But Moses said to God, "Who am I to go to Pharaoh, and to bring the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt?"
en.R: But Moses said to God, "I am not important enough to go to Pharaoh. How can I lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt?"

decisions.choice: who am I: a question that means "I am not fit for this"
decisions.reason: The question is a protest, not a request for information. It is the first of five objections Moses makes (3:11, 13; 4:1, 10, 13). David asks the same question in 2 Samuel 7:18.

decisions.choice: I am not important enough
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the question plainly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כִּֽי־אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י שְׁלַחְתִּ֑יךָ בְּהוֹצִֽיאֲךָ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם תַּֽעַבְדוּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, for I will be with you, and this [will be] for you the sign that I sent you: when you bring out the people from Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "For I will be with you; and this [will be] the sign for you that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain."
en.B: God answered, "I will be with you. And this will be your proof that I am the one who sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will all worship God here on this mountain."
en.R: God said, "I will be with you. Here is how you will know that I have sent you. After you lead the people out of Egypt, all of you will come back here and worship God on this mountain."

decisions.choice: I will be: the verb of the name in verse 14
decisions.reason: "I will be with you" uses the same verb form that God uses of himself in verse 14. The answer to Moses' "Who am I?" is not who Moses is, but who will be with him.

decisions.choice: this will be the sign: the sign comes after the event
alternatives: the burning bush is the sign
decisions.reason: The sign is the worship on this mountain, which can come only after the exodus. It may be a sign that confirms afterward, or "this" may point back to the burning bush as the present sign. The first reading fits the words best.

decisions.choice: you will serve God: worship him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Israel's forced labor for Egypt (1:13-14). Israel will move from serving Pharaoh to serving God (4:23; 7:16).

decisions.choice: you will all / all of you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural: Moses and the people. Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֣י בָא֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לָהֶ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְאָֽמְרוּ־לִ֣י מַה־שְּׁמ֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to God, look, I [am] coming to [the] sons of Israel and I say to them, [the] God of your fathers has sent me to you, and they say to me, what [is] his name? What shall I say to them?

en.L: And Moses said to God, "Look, I am coming to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and I will say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they will say to me, 'What [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What shall I say to them?"
en.B: Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What answer am I to give them?"
en.R: Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and say, 'The God of your ancestors has sent me to you.' They will ask me, 'What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name?' What should I tell them?"

decisions.choice: what is his name: who is he, what is he like
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "what" with a name asks about its meaning, the character of the one named. The people want to know who this God is and what he will do.

decisions.choice: your fathers: the forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The plural refers to the ancestors of Israel, named in verse 15.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽהְיֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Moses, I will be who I will be. And he said, thus you shall say to [the] sons of Israel, I will be has sent me to you.

en.L: And God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Thus you shall say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'I AM has sent me to you.'"
en.B: God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this: 'I AM has sent me to you.'"
en.R: God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM. Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'The one called I AM has sent me to you.'"

decisions.choice: I am who I am: God's name explained from the verb "to be"
alternatives: I will be who I will be
I am the one who is (Septuagint)
I will be what I will be
decisions.reason: The divine name in verse 15 sounds like this verb. The Hebrew verb form can mean "I am" or "I will be", so the phrase may mean "I am who I am" (God is who he is, not defined by anything else), "I will be who I will be" (God will show who he is by what he does), or "I am the one who is" (the Septuagint). Verse 12, "I will be with you", uses the same form and points to God's presence with his people. The words are kept as close to the Hebrew as possible so that the reader can weigh these senses.

decisions.choice: I AM has sent me: the verb is used as a name
decisions.reason: The first word of the phrase stands alone as the name of the one who sends Moses. In verse 15 God gives the name itself, which sounds like it.

decisions.choice: I AM WHO I AM; I AM
decisions.reason: Capitals mark the words as God's name, as "LORD" is marked. The present tense is kept as the best-known English form; the footnote gives "I will be".

decisions.choice: the one called I AM
decisions.reason: Readable says that "I AM" is used as a name.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ע֨וֹד אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כֹּֽה־תֹאמַר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם זֶה־שְּׁמִ֣י לְעֹלָ֔ם וְזֶ֥ה זִכְרִ֖י לְדֹ֥ר דֹּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said again God to Moses, thus you shall say to [the] sons of Israel, Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, [the] God of Abraham, [the] God of Isaac and [the] God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This [is] my name forever, and this [is] my remembrance to generation [and] generation.

en.L: And God said further to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever, and this [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} remembrance from generation to generation.
en.B: God also told Moses, "Say this to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, has sent me to you.' That is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name for all time, the name by which I am to be remembered in every generation.
en.R: God also said to Moses, "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, has sent me to you. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever. People in every generation will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by this name.

decisions.choice: Yahweh: the personal name of God
decisions.reason: The four letters of the name sound like the verb "to be" of verse 14, and may mean "he is" or "he causes to be". Out of reverence, Jews came to read it aloud as "Lord" (Adonai). The exact pronunciation is not certain; "Yahweh" is the usual scholarly form.

decisions.choice: my remembrance: the name by which I am to be called on
decisions.reason: "Remembrance" is the name spoken in worship (Psalm 135:13; Hosea 12:5). This name is to be used for all generations.

decisions.choice: this is my name forever: the name is given for all time
decisions.reason: God's name is not a secret to be kept; it is given to his people to use.

decisions.choice: the LORD; with the setting, Yahweh
decisions.reason: The name is written "the LORD" by default, following the long tradition of reading it as "Lord". The divine name setting gives "Yahweh".

source.text: לֵ֣ךְ וְאָֽסַפְתָּ֞ אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵהֶם֙ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִרְאָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם יִצְחָ֥ק וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר פָּקֹ֤ד פָּקַ֨דְתִּי֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הֶעָשׂ֥וּי לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Go, and gather [the] elders of Israel and say to them, Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, has appeared to me, [the] God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, visiting I have visited you and what is done to you in Egypt,

en.L: Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, "I have surely visited you and [seen] what is done to you in Egypt,
en.B: Go and call together the elders of Israel and tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, appeared to me. He said, "I have come to your aid, and I have taken note of how you are treated in Egypt.
en.R: Go and bring together the leaders of Israel. Tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, came to me. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He said, "I have been watching over you. I have seen how the Egyptians are treating you.

decisions.choice: visiting I have visited: I have come to your aid; I have taken note of you
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, for good or ill; here it is to come and help. Joseph's dying words used the same doubled verb: "God will surely visit you" (Genesis 50:24-25). God's words now fulfil Joseph's promise.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of families and clans
decisions.reason: Older men who led the families and spoke for the people.

decisions.choice: Genesis 50:24-25
decisions.reason: Joseph made his brothers swear to carry his bones out of Egypt when God "visited" them. Moses will do so (13:19).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says what the elders were, since "elders" can suggest only old age.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר אַעֲלֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶם֮ מֵעֳנִ֣י מִצְרַיִם֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: and I have said, I will bring you up from [the] affliction of Egypt to [the] land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, to [a] land flowing [with] milk and honey.

en.L: and I have said, I will bring you up from the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, to a land flowing [with] milk and honey."'
en.B: I have resolved to lead you up from your suffering in Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey."'
en.R: I have promised to take you away from the troubles you have in Egypt. I will bring you to the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live. It is a rich land, full of milk and honey."'

decisions.choice: I have said: I have decided, I have promised
decisions.reason: "Say" here means to decide or to declare a purpose.

source.text: וְשָׁמְע֖וּ לְקֹלֶ֑ךָ וּבָאתָ֡ אַתָּה֩ וְזִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֗יִם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽעִבְרִיִּים֙ נִקְרָ֣ה עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה נֵֽלֲכָה־נָּ֞א דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְנִזְבְּחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will listen to your voice, and you will go, you and [the] elders of Israel, to [the] king of Egypt, and you will say to him, Yahweh, [the] God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now let us go, please, [a] journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Yahweh our God.

en.L: And they will listen to your voice; and you and the elders of Israel shall go to the king of Egypt and say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. And now, please let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.'
en.B: They will listen to you. Then you and the elders of Israel are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, has come to meet us. Now please allow us to make a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.'
en.R: The leaders will listen to you. Then you and the leaders must go to the king of Egypt. Tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, has come to us. Please let us travel three days into the desert. We must offer sacrifices there to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, our God.'

decisions.choice: has met with us: has come to meet us
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a chance or appointed meeting. It explains to Pharaoh why Israel must go.

decisions.choice: a journey of three days: a request for a short time away
decisions.reason: The request is modest and fits the custom of going to a holy place to sacrifice. Pharaoh's refusal of even this shows how hard he is (5:2). The text does not say that the request is a trick; God has said from the start that Israel will leave for good (verses 8, 17).

decisions.choice: the Hebrews: the name the Egyptians knew Israel by
decisions.reason: When speaking to Pharaoh, Israel uses the name foreigners use (see 1:15).

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֠י לֹֽא־יִתֵּ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֛ם מֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרַ֖יִם לַהֲלֹ֑ךְ וְלֹ֖א בְּיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I know that will not permit you [the] king of Egypt to go, and not by [a] strong hand.

en.L: But I know that the king of Egypt will not permit you to go, not even by a strong hand.
en.B: I know, though, that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless he is forced by a mighty hand.
en.R: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless he is forced to.

decisions.choice: and not by a strong hand: unless forced by a mighty power
alternatives: not even under pressure from a strong hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "not even by a strong hand", which may mean that no human force will move him. The Septuagint reads "except by a strong hand", which fits verse 20, where God himself acts with his hand. The sense chosen follows the context: Pharaoh will let them go only when God's power forces him.

decisions.choice: a strong hand: great power
decisions.reason: The "strong hand" is the phrase for God's power in bringing Israel out (6:1; 13:9; Deuteronomy 26:8).

source.text: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֤י אֶת־יָדִי֙ וְהִכֵּיתִ֣י אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹל֙ נִפְלְאֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן יְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in its midst, and after that he will send you away.

en.L: So I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and strike Egypt with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wonders that I will do in its midst; and after that he will send you away.
en.B: So I will reach out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and strike Egypt with every kind of wonder that I will do there. Then at last he will send you away.
en.R: So I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great power against Egypt. I will do many amazing things there to punish the Egyptians. After that, the king will let you go.

decisions.choice: my wonders: the plagues
decisions.reason: The "wonders" are the extraordinary acts of chapters 7-12, done by God's power.

decisions.choice: I will stretch out ... he will send you away: the same verb
decisions.reason: "Stretch out" and "send away" are the same Hebrew verb. When God sends out his hand, Pharaoh will send out Israel.

decisions.choice: use my great power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of stretching out the hand.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה בְּעֵינֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י תֵֽלֵכ֔וּן לֹ֥א תֵלְכ֖וּ רֵיקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give [the] favor of this people in [the] eyes of Egypt, and it will be, when you go, you will not go empty.

en.L: And I will give this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians; and it shall be that when you go, you will not go empty.
en.B: I will make the Egyptians look kindly on this people, so that when you leave, you will not go away with nothing.
en.R: I will make the Egyptians feel kindly toward {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. So when you leave Egypt, you will not leave with nothing.

decisions.choice: you will not go empty: as God promised Abraham
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:14 promised that Abraham's descendants would come out of slavery "with great possessions". The law later says that a freed slave is not to be sent away empty-handed (Deuteronomy 15:13).

source.text: וְשָׁאֲלָ֨ה אִשָּׁ֤ה מִשְּׁכֶנְתָּהּ֙ וּמִגָּרַ֣ת בֵּיתָ֔הּ כְּלֵי־כֶ֛סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּשְׂמָלֹ֑ת וְשַׂמְתֶּ֗ם עַל־בְּנֵיכֶם֙ וְעַל־בְּנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְנִצַּלְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall ask [each] woman from her neighbor and from [the one] sojourning [in] her house articles of silver and articles of gold and clothing, and you shall put [them] on your sons and on your daughters, and you shall plunder Egypt.

en.L: And each woman shall ask of her neighbor and of the woman staying in her house articles of silver and articles of gold and clothing; and you shall put [them] on your sons and on your daughters. So you shall plunder the Egyptians."
en.B: Every woman is to ask her Egyptian neighbor, and any woman lodging in her house, for silver and gold jewelry and for clothing. You will dress your sons and daughters in them, and so you will strip Egypt of its wealth."
en.R: Each Israelite woman should ask her Egyptian neighbors, and any Egyptian women living in her house, for things made of silver and gold, and for clothes. You will put these things on your sons and daughters. In this way you will take away the riches of Egypt."

decisions.choice: ask: request, and receive as a gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask. The Egyptians give freely because God has made them favorable (verse 21; 12:35-36). It is not borrowing with a promise to return.

decisions.choice: plunder Egypt: take its wealth as spoil
decisions.reason: The word is used of stripping a defeated enemy. Israel leaves as a victor carrying spoil, not as fleeing slaves; God wins the battle, not Israel.

decisions.choice: the one sojourning in her house: an Egyptian woman lodging in an Israelite home
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a resident foreigner (2:22). It suggests that Israelites and Egyptians lived side by side.

decisions.choice: Egyptian neighbor
decisions.reason: The neighbors are Egyptians, as 12:35-36 shows. Balanced and Readable say so.
